answer: Dear Captain, To ensure we are on the same page, here is a summary of the case: We understand that when moving between “G” deck to “B” deck, the connection is unstable, and WiFi access points appear to be in normal status. At this stage, the issue is not related to Xchange, since if so, all crews at all decks will be affected. Next, please advise: 1 Do you encounter such issue when you remain on both decks, without movement? If the issue is due to a particular WiFi hot spot, then the error shall appear even if you stay on the same deck 2 When you got the 'failed to connect to Xchange" error, please check the WiFi signal on your mobile device. If you lose the connection around the same spot, then it can be a local WiFi coverage issue onboard If you have a laptop available, we can test a bit further than item 2: - Connect the laptop to Xchange WiFi, you don't have to login. - Press windows Start button. Type "cmd" in the search bar, and click on cmd.exe in the search result. A black window shall pop up - Type command "ping 10.0.2.1 -t", then press Enter. Screenshot attached below for your reference. If you get "Reply from 10.0.2.1: bytes 32 xxx ms" in the black window. That means you should be able to connect to Xchange home page. If the result is "Request time out" like below, that means Xchange is not reachable, and you most likely will get the "failed to connect" error. So you can bring the laptop and move between the decks, to monitor when you get the "request timed out", to tell exactly when you lose the access to Xchange.

answer: Dear Captain / Waterway team, ACU passed all diagnostic tests previously. Dash "-" means a particular test was not required and skipped. Per the tracert test, there is another device between the PC and Xchange LAN 1. Let's try direct connection. Connect a PC directly to Xchange LAN 2, and then configure its IP as DHCP per below: 1)On the PC, Click the Start button (in left down corner of the screen), and then click on Control Panel. 2)In the search box, type Network and Sharing Center, select Network and Sharing Center from search results, then click on Change adapter settings 3)Right-click the connection we need to change, most frequently called "Local Area Connection" or "Ethernet", and then click Properties. 4)Click the Networking tab. Under This connection uses the following items, is a list of options. Click on Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) and then click Properties. 5) Check "Obtain an IP address automatically" and Obtain DNS server address automatically" 6)Click OK button and next Close button. Then open web browser, and test if you can reach Xchange at or If the above works, and you can activate IOP in Xchange, then we can remotely troubleshoot VSAT. If it still doesn't work, please follow the below procedure to download the ACU log. Below On the front panel of Antenna Control Unit, there are 2 USB ports, hidden under plastic cover on the left side. 1. Connect USB flash drive to USB port DN on the Antenna Control Unit. 2. If screen does not automatically go to [[VESSEL]] menu, keep pressing right arrow button until you reach that menu. 3. In [[VESSEL]] press up or down arrow button to select [VESSEL]. 4. Press OK button to start copying. 5. Copy progress in percentages will be shown on the display. 6. Once it is finished remove the USB flash drive. 7. Antenna logs will be stored in folder Intellian/Logs/ File name of the logs has following structure X_YYYYMMDD_hhmmss X - type of log, this can have following values: G, M, O, S, R and T YYYY - year MM - month DD - day hh - hour mm - minutes ss - seconds R and T logs do not follow this name structure. Please zip the files for last 1 week (based on the timestamp in file name) and send it to us. Thank you.

question: Hi Thales, Thank you very much for your clarification. I would like to rephrase Selva’s earlier question for better context. The main concern is, what happens if the user is accessing the application from one of the shipboard computers, and the computer login account used is a local Active Directory account such as "Master"? Please keep in mind that any outbound traffic from shipboard computers to the public internet is routed through the ship’s local Fortigate firewall. This firewall traffic is then forwarded to the Xchange Box device and utilizes the “firewall” account. This account is configured to prioritize “Sealink” as the primary connection with “Starlink” as the secondary route. Given this setup, is it technically possible for the DigiDoc application to be accessed using the “Starlink” connection from a shipboard computer, considering the account and routing details provided? Your insights on this would be appreciated so we can understand the behaviour and adjust configurations accordingly if needed. Many thanks. Robert
answer: Hi Robert, In normal circumstance, if Captain logins his Master account from a non-machine PC, then he shall see a green "Connect" button on the top of page, to establish internet access. And then, data from his PC will follow the rules as defined for "Captain" group. However, if he logins on a Machine computer, then he will not see such button, but only a message saying "Session already started". That means data from the PC will still follow the defined rules for "Machine" group, going through the "firewall" and etc, as you mentioned. Thus, using Master account on a Machine PC will not change its device priority (Sealink v.s. Starlink) or firewall rules. If possible, Captain can use a his Master account on a non-machine PC to use Starlink for DigiDoc app. Or,if such app has to run on a machine PC, we can link you with your Marlink Service Manager and technical team, to review the fleet IT design. I'm sure they can find a solution to this. Thank you.

question: [VESSEL] - ATAGOSAN - Starlink Usage Dear Service Desk, Customer received a notification indicating that 350GB of Starlink data (250GB allowance +100GB top up) has been used. However, according to the XChange system on board, the Starlink usage is reported as only 314.3GB. Could you kindly investigate the discrepancy of over 30GB on ATAGOSAN? Inside Sales HK
answer: Good day, There are a few factors that contribute to discrepancy. First of all, Xchange traffic log use GiB, while P360 displays Starlink quota in GB. For example, 314 GiB in Xchange log is equal to 337GB. Secondly, Starlink has background traffic for the antenna and GPS management, which is not included in XChange log, as such traffic does not pass through Xchange. Finally, such discrepancy is also due to the packet retransmission over the satellite link, since such traffic is not counted in XChange log, but in Starlink log. Thank you.

Configuration steps: 1)Click the Start button (in left down corner of the screen), and then click on Control Panel. 2)In the search box, type Network and Sharing Center, select Network and Sharing Center from search results, then click on Change adapter settings 3)Right-click the connection we need to change, most frequently called "Local Area Connection" or "Ethernet", and then click Properties. 4)Click the Networking tab. Click on Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) and then click Properties. 5) Check "Obtain an IP address automatically" and Obtain DNS server address automatically" 6)Click OK button and next Close button. Thank you.

question: Xchange Data usage while logged off Good day, One of our crew members has a strange situation regarding data usage on his exchange account. He previously had issues with connecting to the crew internet via xchange-box.com, then after unsuccessful use of the Xchange app, finally it was installed and working correctly. But, for some reason there is data usage on his account even when logged out, and Wi-Fi deselected on his device. He is only using this account on his mobile phone, a Samsung S24FE with android 14. After going to use apps, when he wants to go back to the Xchange data app to disconnect it is always showing the white page. See attachment. When checking then on the browser page, also no page is coming up. Then he disconnects from Wi-Fi, connects again, and reopens the app. Then he presses ‘’refresh’’ and then the ‘’failed to connect to Xchange’’ message comes up. The strangest part is that data is still being consumed on his account even when he completely closes down his Wi-Fi connection. We reset the account for good measure and only he has the password and only in use on his phone. We look forward to any assistance you can provide. If issue still remains, then there are a few things to clarify: - I presume there are other crews connected to the same WiFi hotspot, and they are not affected? - Please test the same account on a personal PC, then he can login via web browser and test if the same symptom persists. answer: Dear Captain, The numbers displayed in Xchange and backend system are not exactly the same, and there are a few factors that contribute to discrepancy: First of all, Xchange traffic log use GiB, while backend uses displays quota in GB, and 1GiB=1.074 GB, so that is about 7% difference. Secondly, Starlink has background traffic for the antenna and GPS management, which is not included in XChange log, as such traffic does not pass through Xchange. Finally, such discrepancy is also due to the packet retransmission over the satellite link, since such traffic is not counted in XChange log, but in Starlink log. Thank you.

You should reach Certus web interface. To log in , go to administration menu, username : admin, and password is written on the sticker on Certus terminal (example attached below). answer: Dear Captain, You can check the starlink data consumption per screenshot below. The numbers displayed in Xchange and backend system are not exactly the same, and there are a few factors that contribute to discrepancy: First of all, Xchange traffic log use GiB, while backend uses displays quota in GB, and 1GiB=1.074 GB, so that is about 7% difference. Secondly, Starlink has background traffic for the antenna and GPS management, which is not included in XChange log, as such traffic does not pass through Xchange. Finally, such discrepancy is also due to the packet retransmission over the satellite link, since such traffic is not counted in XChange log, but in Starlink log. Thank you.

answer: Dear Captain, That is a good question, and I'll try my best to explain this. Starlink uses a "cell" concept in their system, which is very similar to our GSM mobile network. Basically, cell is the smallest coverage unit, which starlink applies restriction rules on. Please refer to below screenshots, your cell number: [PHONE]fffffff; GH Challenger cell number: [PHONE]b3fffffff. So from Starlink point of view, your good vessel and GH Challenger are under the coverage of different cells. In this case, your vessel is considered under Angola water, while GH Challenger is not. Thus, Starlink may apply different restriction rules. This is solely controlled by Starlink, and we can't change it. Hopefully this clarifies your doubt, and please feel free to contact us shall you have further questions. Thank you.

question: Hi Good Day! For the Crew Internet and wifi access, kindly share the details for POE wifi routers and what is the power supply setup required for this. Kindly share the WIfi router configuration details as well for DNS, Primary DNS, Secondary DNS etc along with IP address setup. Which ports in Xchange Port to be connected for Crew wifi setup. Nischey Chopra Sr. Technical Superintendent [VESSEL],LTD 7 Jalan Kilang #03-01 Singapore [PHONE] HP: [PHONE] EMAIL:
answer: Good day, Crew WIFi can be connected to XChange LAN 2. There is no specific requirement about the WiFi device. It can be on POE, or with standalone power supply, depending on whether your switch supports POE. The only important thing is, WiFi device must be in Access Point mode, not Router. In other words, the WiFi device shouldn't perform IP translation, and crew device should get IP assigned by XChange, not by WIFi device itself. For your reference, we use D-Link AC2300 access point. Current LAN 2 IP is: 10.128.77.41/29, with DHCP disabled. If you intend to use LAN 2 for crew WIFi, we'd recommend to set a larger subnet, and have DHCP enabled. If you don't have access to update that yet, please advise the intended configuration, and we can update that for you. If you'd like to use static IP on LAN 2, then you can use XChange [VESSEL].128.77.41 as gateway and DNS. Thank you.

question: (#[PHONE]) Inquiry About Data Allocation Across Laurel Fleet -#-#- Please reply above this line -#-#- Dear [EMAIL], A new ticket has been created on your behalf. You can add a comment by replying to this email. Ticket Details Ticket #: [PHONE] Subject: Inquiry About Data Allocation Across Laurel Fleet Department: IT Support and Trainings Status: Open Priority: Normal Shashank Singh Staff - Tuesday 25th February 2025 22:23 Dear Team, Good Day! Regarding the subject matter, could you please clarify the breakdown of data allocation across different service types for the box users. For example, in the Crew group settings on the Marlink Portal for the vessel Firando , we observed that the Daily Credit for Crew is set to 10 ($/€), providing 1,000 MB (Data) on Starlink and 1,000 MB(Data) on Sealink (refer to screenshot no. 1). Given this setup, we would like to confirm, when Starlink is un﻿available, will the crew be able to fully utilize 1,000 MB of data on VSAT (Sealink). If we change the channel preference, setting Sealink as priority 1 and Starlink as priority 2 (refer to screenshot no. 2), will the crew be able >> First consume 1,000 MB on VSAT (Sealink) >> Then, switch to 1,000 MB on Starlink once VSAT data is exhausted As per our communication with Laurel Office, the vessel crew should receive a total of 1 GB/day across both VSAT and Starlink. This would ensure that vessels in non-Starlink zones can seamlessly use VSAT without facing restrictions. Please advise so we can update Laurel Office accordingly. Thanks & Regards, Mr. Shashank Singh Associate Engineer - Technical Support Vertex Infosoft Solutions Pvt. Ltd. Shift Timings: 0900 to 1830 (IST) (Mon-Fri) Mobile: [PHONE] 24x7 line: [PHONE] [EMAIL] Attachments (54.2 KB) (52.9 KB) You can review the ticket by going Kind Regards, Vertex Infosoft
answer: Good day, To address your questions: - "when Starlink is un﻿available, will the crew be able to fully utilize 1,000 MB of data on VSAT (Sealink). " Marlink: Yes. If Starlink is not available, then Xchange will switch to Sealink, and crew shall be able to consume all the $10 allowance on Sealink, which is equivalent to 1000MB. - "If we change the channel preference, setting Sealink as priority 1 and Starlink as priority 2 (refer to screenshot no. 2), will the crew be able >> First consume 1,000 MB on VSAT (Sealink) >> Then, switch to 1,000 MB on Starlink once VSAT data is exhausted" Marlink : No. There are two reasons: firstly, after a crew consumes 1000 MB on VSAT, he will have depleted all $10, and have no allowance left; secondly, as long as VSAT is online, crew doesn't have the option to choose to switch to Starlink. Thus, even if he still has allowance left, he can only continue to surf on VSAT but not on Starlink. To meet your requirement that " crew should receive a total of 1 GB/day across both VSAT and Starlink", you may consider issue each crew two accounts, one for Starlink and one for Sealink. Then crew can choose which one to use at his convenience. Thank you.

question: WO status issue (Please forward to SMMS-[VESSEL] addressed persons!!) Good day, Attached an example which shows exactly why we are facing struggles in parts of our administration. As I’ve mentioned earlier the incorrect roles hierarchy (which has been explained later by the team), this WO shows very well where partly the unpleasant experience in my role occurs. · Situation: A WO made for the renewal of two evaporators at our chiller units. Consisting of 8 tasks. Partly the WO is in progress (physically). Undersigned needs to enter the WO for administrative reason. · What happened: One engineer already marked several tasks as <technical complete> due to the fact it has been executed. So the man did what he is expected to do, keep administration up to date. · Result: I, as CE, want to add task lines because of different follow-up in reality. Impossible, because status is in <Running>……………. Booking of parts, once tasks are in <technical complete> is still possible. · Issue: I can’t reverse the status change of the tasks back to pending. In this case necessary because the engineer made accidently a mistake in sequence. (Chiller 2 is done, not chiller 1). The entire WO has changed to <running> because of the action of the engineer. So tasks still in <pending> are also blocked for changes (other than change those status as well). I can’t add text or what so ever. ONLY until status <technical complete> is reached. A very likely result of all this can be that we have to keep WO’s as long as possible in draft. This will create for sure an enormous pile of administrative mess. Moreover also due to the fact that more than one person are working administratively in the same WO. Everybody involved does his part. The explanation I’ve got regarding the hierarchy in roles at the moment has absolute nothing to do with this. Prevention of roles executing things they are not qualified for (according Dolphin team). A chief-engineer (CE), on every vessel of O&E, Dredging, Cables etc. , is end-responsible for the technical administration of executed tasks and jobs. In other words, a CE has to be able to make any change in tasks, writing errors, status change errors of engineers and booking parts until the last step. And that step is closing the WO. This requested change in role has nothing to do with exceptional, additional role possibilities. Just to execute my function as I am expected to do so. Met vriendelijke groet / Allard Zwart Chief Engineer Prins der Nederlanden Royal Boskalis Westminster N.V. answer: Good day, Captain If it's raining or vessel is sailing on rough sea, VSAT antenna may be affected. When sea is clam and it's not raining, please run a diagnostic test on Intellian ACU: 1. Press Menu (M) key on ACU front panel; 2. Press LEFT key to move cursor to YES and press OK key to enter setup mode. 3. Select "ANTENNA" menu, press OK key 4. Press arrow keys to look for "DIAGONOSIS" (it's not on display initially) and press OK key to enter DIAGONOSIS menu 5. Press DOWN arrow key to select "[VESSEL]" option and press OK key to execute it Antenna will then go through a sequence of 15 tests. You will see on ACU display: Solid Dot: means test passed -: means test is not applicable and skipped ? : means under progress Numbers: means a particular test has failed. For example, 2 means test number 2 failed Please wait for all tests to complete, and let us know the outcome of diagnostic test.

question: Xchange 5.6 Good morning I was involved in an Xchange install (4G/Starlink only). The superintendent was very adamant that the crew should be allocated only 1GB data by way of Xchange. When completing the install wizard on the Xchange it was not possible for me to adjust the price matrix at the wizard. When looking through the menues there was nowhere that I could see how to change the tariffs i.e. where the engineer can set the charged prices for the crew making a data session. Everything was in dollars and not in MB in the Xch app. I therefore called the Regional NOC to get an explanation as to how this is achieved but did not receive an answer, rather that I should send an email so this is the reason for this. In the old XCH software the wizard settings could be changed to allow the IOF charging matrix to be true, even in the menu it could be adjusted. In the new software 5.6 this is now not there and in the XCH menues I could not see any way of adjusting any price matrix. How does the superintendent get to have his crew using 1GB data per man and month ? BR/Steve Stephen Hay Sales and Service Manager, Maritime T +46 (0)[PHONE] M +46 (0)[PHONE] E , Digitally advancing your remote world by creating Possibilities. Anywhere.
answer: Hi, Xchange price matrix should be configured in P360, which will be pushed to Xchange box. Although you could configure price in Xchange, it would be overwritten by the settings in P360.
